answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a ferrous-hard deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers catch it copying another agent's work. Honest agents earn the deposit back plus fees, so a real participant keeps a steady pulse of useful transactions, while a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds at once. No haven exists for cheap clones, because each identity pays the same upfront cost.
